'''Edward Gibson Gallrein III''' (born April 20, 1958) is an American farmer and former [[United States Navy SEALs|Navy SEAL]] officer. A member of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], Gallrein is its nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky#District 4|United States House of Representatives election]] for [[Kentucky's 4th congressional district]] in 2026.

Gallrein defeated Republican seven-term incumbent [[Thomas Massie]] in the most expensive primary election in U.S. congressional history, advancing to the general election against [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee Melissa Strange and Libertarian candidate Jeremy Todd. Gallrein was endorsed by [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], with the race largely seen as a referendum on [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump's second presidency]] amid the [[2026 Iran war]].

==Early life and education==
Edward Gibson Gallrein III was born on April 20, 1958.<ref name="LeaderStuart">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/leader-news-stuart-gallrein/197882437/ |title=Stuart-Gallrein |date=November 20, 1985 |work=Leader-News |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="NYTimesInfo">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/19/us/politics/ed-gallrein-kentucky-republican-house-election.html |title=5 Things to Know About the Kentucky House Challenger Ed Gallrein |date=May 19, 2026 |last=Balk |first=Tim |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QKH5-3GCN?lang=en&cid=fs_copy|title=Edward G Gallrein, Kentucky Public Record Indexes, 1911-1999|access-date=May 20, 2026}}</ref> Gallrein is the son of Fay Hays and Edward Gallrein Jr.<ref name="LeaderStuart"/> Gallrein's father was a farmer in [[Logan County, Kentucky]], and Gallrein grew up on the family farm.<ref>[https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/who-is-ed-gallrein-navy-seal-and-farmer-who-could-oust-thomas-massie-in-kentucky/ar-AA23va8x "Who is Ed Gallrein? Navy SEAL and farmer who could oust Thomas Massie in Kentucky,"] MSN, May 18, 2026.</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-in-harvest/197882407/ |title=In harvest... |date=October 14, 1979 |last=Norman |first=Phil |work=[[Courier Journal]] |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> Gallrein himself is a fifth-generation Kentucky farmer.<ref>[https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/19/politics/ed-gallrein-thomas-massie-donald-trump-kentucky-election "Kentucky voters make their choice today: Thomas Massie, or a former Navy SEAL picked by Trump to beat him,"] CNN,  May 19, 2026.</ref>

Gallrein graduated from [[Franklin-Simpson High School]] in 1975. He attended [[Centre College]], where he played varsity football for the [[Centre Colonels football|Centre Colonels]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pmg-ky1.com/sentinel_news/gallrein-inducted-into-the-franklin-simpson-athletic-hall-of-fame/article_5e41f466-9466-564d-b632-05a0f435476d.html |title=Gallrein Inducted into the Franklin-Simpson Athletic Hall of Fame |date=November 7, 2024 |work=The Sentinel News |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> Gallrein then graduated from [[Murray State University]] with a bachelor's degree in Agriculture in 1981, and a Master of Science in Agriculture - Agribusiness Economics in 1984.<ref name="LoganOther">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-logan-leader-the-other-day/197882937/ |title=the other day... |date=August 10, 1981 |work=The Logan Leader |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="LeaderStuart"/> He played football for the [[Murray State Racers football|Murray State Racers]].<ref name="LoganOther"/>

He later attended the [[Naval Postgraduate School]] where he received a Master of Science in [[Financial Management]] with honors. He then attended the [[Air War College]] where he received a Master of Strategic Studies degree with distinction.<ref>[https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/588138/Edward_Gibson_Gallrein_III.html "Ed Gallrein ,"] Legistorm.</ref>

==Military career==
[[File:Ed Gallrein.jpg|left|thumb|233x233px|Gallrein in 2014]]
Gallrein served in the U.S. military for three decades,  from 1984 to 2014, serving with [[U.S. Navy]] [[SEAL Team Six]]. He rose to the rank of Navy [[Captain (United States O-6)|captain]], as he was deployed to [[Operation Just Cause|Panama]], [[Operation Enduring Freedom|Afghanistan]], [[Operation Iraqi Freedom|Iraq]], and the [[Persian Gulf]].<ref>[https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/05/20/ed-gallrein-defeated-incumbent-rep-thomas-massie-in-the-republican-primary-for-kentuckys-4th-congressional-district-on-may-19-2026/ "Ed Gallrein defeated incumbent Rep. Thomas Massie in the Republican primary for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District on May 19, 2026"], Ballotpedia, May 20, 2026.</ref><ref name="NYTimesInfo"/><ref name="spectrum">{{cite news|url=https://spectrumnews1.com/ky/louisville/news/2025/10/21/ed-gallrein-thomas-massie|title=Trump-endorsed candidate, Ed Gallrein, announces candidacy|work=Spectrum News|date=October 21, 2025}}</ref>

He was inspired to join the military by President [[Ronald Reagan]].<ref name="NYTimesInfo"/> By November 1985, Gallrein had become an [[Ensign (rank)|ensign]] in the [[United States Navy]] and was stationed at [[Joint Expeditionary Base–Little Creek|Little Creek Naval Amphibious Base]].<ref name="LeaderStuart"/> During his 2026 political campaign, Gallrein said that he had received four [[Bronze Star Medal]]s; Gallrein was awarded three—the fourth appears to be the bronze star on his [[Parachutist Badge (United States)|Combat Parachutist Badge]].<ref name="Beast">{{cite news|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/ed-gallrein-melts-down-as-right-wing-outlet-turns-on-him/|title=MAGA Candidate Melts Down as Right-Wing Outlet Turns on Him|work=Daily Beast|date=18 May 2026|last=Esposito|first=Laura}}</ref>   He also has two [[Presidential Unit Citation (United States)|Presidential Unit Citations]].<ref name="yahoo">{{cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/kentucky-primary-race-between-massie-090252870.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAGZ0hRDNLe-KHM1PnwKSH3KlzpHsYHkGYGar64nFg8f-S50P0EahO0DrbecrC9-DXzk0Ijyh47YK9dZ9StBF87bEgLOWUQhzztC2taVsTJ4ks_FIsjWjjHt71XmZ-blIyyUWYTv0U3pkQTlesxrNJbnL8VOgNFV1pG6Dmz66b2la|title=Kentucky primary race between Massie and Gallrein for Congress is one to watch|work=Yahoo|date=May 15, 2026 }}</ref>

After his military career, Gallrein turned to becoming a [[dairy farmer]] and a business owner operating Circle G Farm and Stables in Shelby County since 2014.<ref name="ballotpedia">{{Cite web |title=Ed Gallrein |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Ed_Gallrein |access-date=2026-10-07 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/19/us/politics/thomas-massie-primary-kentucky.html "Massie Is Defeated in Kentucky, Falling to a Trump-Backed Challenger"], ''The New York Times'', May 19, 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.thetimes.com/us/news-today/article/who-is-ed-gallrein-trump-kentucky-primary-550ptb0lj "Who is Ed Gallrein? The Trump-picked victor in Kentucky's primary"], ''The Times'',  May 20, 2026.</ref>

==Political career==
===2024 Kentucky Senate campaign===
{{See also|2024 Kentucky Senate election#District 7}}
On August 17, 2023, Gallrein announced that he would run in the [[2024 Kentucky Senate election]] for the state's [[Kentucky's 7th Senate district|7th district]] as a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pmg-ky1.com/sentinel_news/edward-gallrein-announces-bid-for-kentucky-state-senate/article_068c7b56-3fab-50a1-bd54-5463d04edb53.html |title=Edward Gallrein announces bid for Kentucky State Senate |date=August 17, 2023 |last=Lacer |first=Bobby |work=The Sentinel-News |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> By April 2024, he had garnered $169,000, largely from operatives within the [[Republican Party of Kentucky]], including its former chairman, Mac Brown; donor Wayne Hunt; and [[Michael Adams (Kentucky politician)|Michael Adams]], the state's [[Secretary of State of Kentucky|secretary of state]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kentucky.com/news/politics-government/article287982110.html |title=KY primaries are here. Which statehouse races to watch, how much campaigns are raising |date=April 25, 2024 |last=Horn |first=Austin |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref>

Gallrein lost the Republican nomination to [[Aaron Reed]] by 118 votes (39.3% to 38.3%).<ref name=ballotpedia/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kentucky.com/news/politics-government/article288695735.html |title=Checking the math: Elections officials to closely review ballot totals in two races |date=May 24, 2024 |last=Horn |first=Austin |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> Gallrein requested a recanvass, which reaffirmed Reed's victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kentucky.com/news/politics-government/article288882268.html |title=Narrow KY statehouse wins stand with 'no changes' to primary races recanvassed |date=May 30, 2024 |last=Horn |first=Austin |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref>

===2026 U.S. House of Representatives campaign===
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky#District 4}}
[[File:POTUS at Verst Logistics Manufacturing in Kentucky - P20260311JB-1717.jpg|thumb|Gallrein with U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] at Verst Logistics Manufacturing in [[Hebron, Kentucky]]]]
[[File:EGFC.jpg|thumb|Political sign for Ed Gallrein]]
[[File:2026_Kentucky's_4th_congressional_district_Republican_primary_election_results_by_county.svg|thumb|2026 Republican primary results by county:{{collapsible list
| title = {{legend|#5FD3BC|Gallrein}}|{{legend|#5FD3BC|50–60%}}|{{legend|#2ca089|60–70%}}
}}{{collapsible list
| title = {{legend|#E27F7F|Massie}}|{{legend|#E27F7F|50–60%}}|{{legend|#D75D5D|60–70%}}
}}]]
On October 17, 2025, President [[Donald Trump]] endorsed Gallrein for [[Kentucky's congressional districts|Kentucky's 4th congressional district]].<ref name="ballotpedia" /> On October 21, Gallrein announced his candidacy for the [[United States House of Representatives]], challenging seven-term incumbent [[Thomas Massie]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky#Republican primary 4|Republican primary]].<ref>[https://cartercountytimes.com/editorials/editorial/president-trump-wasnt-about-to-lose-in-the-fourth-district/ "President Trump wasn’t about to lose in the Fourth District"], ''Carter County Times'', May 27, 2026.</ref> Massie had held the seat since 2012 and was considered to be popular within the district; in 2024, he had won the Republican primary with 76% of the vote and the general election with 99.6% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web |title=November 5, 2024 Official 2024 General Election Results |url=https://elect.ky.gov/results/2020-2029/Documents/2024%20General%20Election%20Certification%20as%20Amended%20on%20December%209th%202024.pdf |website=elect.ky.gov |publisher=[[Kentucky Secretary of State]] |access-date=January 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250116091107/https://elect.ky.gov/results/2020-2029/Documents/2024%20General%20Election%20Certification%20as%20Amended%20on%20December%209th%202024.pdf |archive-date=January 16, 2025 |page=13 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schreiner |first=Bruce |date=2025-10-21 |title=Trump-endorsed candidate enters race to challenge Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky |url=https://apnews.com/article/trump-massie-gallrein-congressional-campaign-3926a623a521302d7b33eac5ddf61a4a |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=AP News}}</ref> However, by March 2025, Trump had openly called for a primary challenge to Massie in response to his votes on the [[2025 United States federal budget|2025 federal budget]].<ref name="massie">{{cite news |author=Walker, Jackson |date=March 11, 2025 |title=Thomas Massie announces reelection bid as Trump vows to back primary challenger |url=https://thenationaldesk.com/news/americas-news-now/thomas-massie-announces-reelection-bid-as-trump-vows-to-back-primary-challenger |access-date=March 11, 2025 |work=[[The National Desk]]}}</ref> Other high-profile clashes between the two included Massie's vote against the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]], his [[Epstein Files Transparency Act|advocacy]] for the release of the [[Epstein files]], and his condemnation of [[2025 United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites|U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Horn, Austin |date=June 22, 2025 |title=KY Rep. Thomas Massie is at odds again with Trump over Iran. Here's the history |url=https://www.kentucky.com/news/politics-government/article309170635.html |access-date=June 22, 2025 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodman |first=Sylvia |date=2026-05-11 |title=Massie or Gallrein? Kentucky voters to decide the true meaning of MAGA in heated GOP primary |url=https://www.lpm.org/news/2026-05-11/massie-or-gallrein-kentucky-voters-to-decide-the-true-meaning-of-maga-in-heated-gop-primary |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=Louisville Public Media |language=en}}</ref>

During the campaign, pro-Massie and pro-Gallrein PACs both used [[AI-generated content in American politics|AI-generated political ads]] to attack each other's campaigns.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 May 2026 |title=The Massie-Gallrein race is not what most people think |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/05/16/thomas-massie-faces-ed-gallrein-kentucky-may-19-primary/90079310007/ |work=Cincinnati.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sonka |first1=Joe |last2=Goodman |first2=Sylvia |date=5 May 2026 |title=AI 'deepfake' ads attack Massie and Gallrein in northern Kentucky GOP primary |url=https://www.lpm.org/news/2026-05-05/ai-deepfake-ads-attack-massie-and-gallrein-in-northern-kentucky-gop-primary |work=Louisville Public Media}}</ref> One AI-generated ad from pro-Gallrein PAC MAGA KY included imagery of Massie having a [[threesome]] with pro-[[Palestine|Palestinian]] Democratic representatives [[Ilhan Omar]] and [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]].<ref name="Omar">{{cite news |last=Delaney |first=Arthur |date=4 May 2026 |title=MAGA Attack Ad Uses AI To Show Thomas Massie 'Cheating With The Squad' |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/thomas-massie-throuple-attack-ad-cheating-squad_n_69f8dca9e4b06e9242f57b3f |work=[[HuffPost]]}}</ref> Massie, Omar, and former Rep. [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]] condemned the ad, with Greene accusing the ad of violating the [[TAKE IT DOWN Act]].<ref name="Omar" /> On May 16, a pro-Trump group announced that Secretary of Defense [[Pete Hegseth]] would visit Kentucky to raise support for Gallrein. Hegseth's move was accused by critics of violating the [[Hatch Act]], which the White House denied.<ref>{{cite news |last=Aitken |first=Peter |date=17 May 2026 |title=Pentagon Defends Hegseth Stumping Against Massie Amid Hatch Act Claims |url=https://www.newsweek.com/pete-hegseth-thomas-massie-ed-gallreinand-hatch-act-violation-11961018 |work=[[Newsweek]]}}</ref> During the campaign, Gallrein declined to debate Massie, ignored most interview requests, and conducted few public rallies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Almendarez |first=Jolene |title=The Massie-Gallrein race is not what most people think |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/05/16/thomas-massie-faces-ed-gallrein-kentucky-may-19-primary/90079310007/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Doll |first=Keely |title=Why Ed Gallrein isn't interested in debating Thomas Massie |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/News/politics/elections/2026/04/10/ed-gallrein-thomas-massie-debate-2026-primary-elections/89543309007/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=The Courier-Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

On May 11, 2026, the primary became the most expensive U.S. House primary in American history, with over $25.6 million in ad spending beating the prior record of $25.2 million from the [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in New York#District 16|Democratic primary]] for [[New York's 16th congressional district]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solender |first=Andrew |date=2026-05-11 |title=Inside the wild $25 million fight to oust top GOP Trump critic Thomas Massie |url=https://www.axios.com/2026/05/11/thomas-massie-ed-gallrein-kentucky-aipac-trump |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref> By May 17, ad spending exceeded $32 million.<ref name="Record">{{cite news |last=Kashinsky |first=Lisa |date=17 May 2026 |title=Massie's primary is the most expensive in history. Pro-Israel groups have played a huge part. |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/17/massie-aipac-record-spending-israel-maga-trump-primary-00925375 |work=Politico}}</ref> Gallrein won the Republican nomination on May 19, 2026, 54.9%–45.1%, winning 19 of the 21 counties that voted.<ref>[https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-elections/kentucky-us-house-district-4-results "Kentucky House District 4 Primary Results 2026,"] NBC News.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Aulbach |first1=Lucas |last2=Johnson |first2=Krista |last3=Kuzydym |first3=Stephanie |last4=Gerth |first4=Joseph |title=KY-4 primary called for Ed Gallrein over Thomas Massie: NBC, DDHQ |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/News/politics/elections/2026/05/19/kentucky-primary-election-2026-results-thomas-massie-ed-gallrein/89809682007/ |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=The Courier-Journal |language=en-US|date=19 May 2026}}</ref> After the race was called in Gallrein's favor, he said: "It was a [[David versus Goliath]]. I was the underdog."<ref>[https://www.foxnews.com/media/trump-backed-candidate-ed-gallrein-calls-kentucky-upset-david-vs-goliath-win-defeating-massie "Kentucky win a ‘David vs. Goliath’ victory after defeating Massie,"] Fox News,  May 20, 2026 .</ref>

Gallrein will face Democrat Melissa Strange in the general election on November 3, 2026.<ref name=ballotpedia/>

== Political positions ==
Gallrein was a registered [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] until May 2016, when he left the party to become an [[Independent politician|independent]]. He rejoined the Republican Party in June 2021.<ref>{{cite news|last=Zimmerman|first=David|url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/4488603/trump-massie-gallrein-past-republican-party-change/|title=Trump defends Massie primary challenger for leaving GOP in past: 'Ed still supported me'|work=Washington Examiner|date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

===Economy and cost of living===
Gallrein supports cutting taxes, reducing regulations, and decreasing government spending.<ref name=ballotpedia/>

===Border control and fentanyl===
Gallein supports [[border enforcement]], fully funding the [[U.S. Border Patrol]] and [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]], completing the [[Mexico–United States border wall]], and putting an end to the flow of illegal drugs such as [[fentanyl]] into the United States and the [[Opioid epidemic in the United States|United States opioid epidemic]].<ref name=ballotpedia/>

===Diversity, equity, and inclusion===
Gallrein is opposed to the idea of [[diversity, equity, and inclusion]] and believes that these principles should be removed from schools, the military, and the government.<ref name=ballotpedia/>

===Second Amendment rights===
Gallrein said that "the [[Second Amendment]] is under constant attack from the radical left" and believes that U.S. citizens should maintain the [[Right to keep and bear arms in the United States|right to keep and bear arms]].<ref name=ballotpedia/>

===Foreign policy===
Gallrein supported the [[2026 United States intervention in Venezuela|2026 U.S. intervention in Venezuela]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schreiner |first=Bruce |date=2026-01-06 |title=Military action in Venezuela emerges as an issue in a closely watched GOP primary in Kentucky |url=https://apnews.com/article/congress-kentucky-massie-gallrein-venezuela-c6942fd0734a2381fd9b1de06f4331de |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

Commenting on the [[2026 Iran War]], Gallrein said on [[X (social network)|X]] on February 28, 2026, that the United States' attack on Iran: "sends a clear message to the world: The United States will not sit back while a hostile regime continually threatens our Nation, our allies, and global stability as Iran has for decades as the leading [[state sponsor of terrorism]] been responsible for the death of U.S. citizens and servicemembers.... Decisive action, clear objectives, and overwhelming strength save American lives and prevent larger wars, death, and destruction."<ref>[https://kentuckylantern.com/2026/02/28/kentucky-republican-thomas-massie-says-he-will-push-for-congressional-vote-on-iran-war/ "Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie says he will push for congressional vote on Iran war,"] Kentucky Lantern, February 28, 2026 .</ref>

==Personal life==
Gallrein lives in [[Shelbyville, Kentucky]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Horsley|first=McKenna|title=Beshear: Trump should have spent Kentucky visit justifying Iran war|date=March 12, 2026|url=https://kentuckylantern.com/2026/03/12/trump-should-have-spent-kentucky-visit-justifying-iran-war/|work=[[Kentucky Lantern]]|access-date=November 1, 2026}}</ref>

In December 1985, Gallrein married Mary E. Stuart.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/leader-news-marriage-licenses/197883641/ |title=Marriage Licenses |date=December 11, 1985 |work=Leader-News |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> According to court filings, Gallrein filed to divorce his second wife, Heather Gallrein,<ref name="about ed">{{Cite news |title=About Ed - Ed Gallrein for State Senate |url=https://votegallrein.com/about/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251020145408/https://votegallrein.com/about/ |archive-date=2025-10-20 |access-date=2026-05-20 |work=Ed Gallrein for State Senate |language=en-US}}</ref> in 2024 (one month after losing the Kentucky state legislature election). According to court filings, he told her to "get out of his house" and decided to cut her off financially. Gallrein has denied this claim.<ref name="Beast"/>
